name: NOMAD
summary: NOMAD searched for tau-neutrino appearance at CERN through final-state kinematics in a low-density magnetic detector, and produced precision neutrino interaction measurements.
physics_targets: Charm, coherent meson production and oscillation constraints
detection_principle: Drift chambers acted as both target and tracker in a dipole magnet. Transition-radiation, preshower and electromagnetic calorimeter systems identified electrons, while muon chambers identified muons. Missing transverse momentum and correlations tested tau decays without directly resolving their short flight.

key_parameters.name: Magnet
key_parameters.value: 0.4 T dipole based on the former UA1 magnet

key_parameters.name: Beam
key_parameters.value: CERN SPS West Area wide-band neutrino facility

results.summary: No tau-appearance signal was established; kinematic analysis supplied strong short-baseline constraints and a broad neutrino-scattering data set.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.
